root_cause: The coverage-complete critic 19 code review (same Opus High worker) passed treatment A and the measured board but returned revise on treatment B with two blocking motion defects. NB1: the B push stretches the right forearm 12 percent at release and 24 percent at the end of the glide while the hand floats off the card. NB2: three fingers snap between poses in a single frame at 0.43 s, 1.80 s and 14.77 s. Independently classified as non-deferrable modern motion floor failures. The independent recurrence pivot review (critic 20) judged an arm solve and finger blend alone to be a defect correction inside the same push mechanism, not a pivot, and recommended changing the performed action. The recurrence pivot reviewer (critic 21) accepted continuous fingertip contact as a genuine change of the performed action but returned revise because a fixed-shoulder two-bone solve cannot reach: in ClinicSupport.tsx the resting arm is already straight (upper arm plus forearm 1470.6 local units, wrist-to-shoulder distance 1470.3), carrying the card to the B tool-mouth lip needs the shoulder about 13 percent beyond full arm length, and the s3 push to the chart edge about 5 percent beyond.
repair: Change treatment B's performed send to a continuous-contact push in which the right fingertip stays on the card's contact point at every frame until the tool-mouth lip occludes the card, never clamped and never released into a glide, with no airborne return. Keep both arm segment lengths constant (rest forearm and upper-arm lengths) and let the shoulder, meaning the torso, lean forward and right with the reach so the solver always reaches the contact point; the shoulder offset is a continuous eased function of the push window and returns smoothly. Blend the finger lift into the reach with an eased lerp. Apply the same lean-and-contact push to B's s3 question push. All gated to treatment b so treatment a pictures stay unchanged. Edit only ClinicAnswerFilm.tsx. Boards, timing, narration, art files, voice, mix and captions are unchanged.
mechanism_change: B's send changes from a release-and-glide push with a stretching elbow to a continuous-contact push carried by a leaning torso with constant limb lengths, so the hand stays attached to the card from touch to occlusion.
expected_visible_result: In B the fingertip stays on the card from first touch until the tool-mouth lip occludes it with no clamp, stretch, release or airborne hand, forearm and upper-arm lengths are constant, the torso lean and finger lift are continuous at 30 fps, and A and the measured selected board render identical pictures.
